title: Multiband Optical and Near-Infrared Properties of Faint Submillimeter Galaxies with Serendipitous ALMA Detections
question: What are the optical/NIR properties, photometric redshifts and colors of faint SMGs serendipitously detected in archival ALMA data in the XMM-LSS field?

data.bands: Band 6 (211-275 GHz) and Band 7 (275-370 GHz); all but one project in Band 6

evidence.quote: The quiescent galaxy color cuts are taken from Williams et al. (2009).
Chen et al. (2016b) have devised a selection technique to identify bright as well as faint SMGs

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image archival ALMA data
recipe.method: Run archive scripts in CASA, CLEAN MFS imaging
PyBDSF positions with threshpix 3.5 sigma; JMFIT Gaussian fit fluxes on PB-corrected maps
Negative peak analysis on maps multiplied by -1
Cross-match ALMA with VIDEO within 1'', Tractor forced photometry on 10'' cutouts, fiducial VIDEO Ks band
EAZY with default templates, zpeak, 95% intervals, 0<z<6

recipe.goal: Stack undetected >5 sigma sources in IRAC
recipe.method: Stack DeepDrill IRAC at positions of 60 undetected >5 sigma sources, split by 1 mJy

evidence.quote: we selected a detection threshold of 3.9 σ for the archival ALMA data.
our ALMA catalog was reduced to 176 objects.
found 26 faint SMGs with counterparts within a search radius of 1 ′′ .
The median redshifts for bands 6 and 7 are ⟨z⟩ = 2.72 and 2.57, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: IRAC 4.5um stack of faint (<1 mJy) undetected sources
